sofia: Heads up — CI perf alert for apac-a10 canary. After yesterday's merge we see ~22% throughput drop and p99 latency up ~45% for text-gen (4k seq). link: https://ci.internal/perf/17498 :rotating_light:
perf-bot: [perf/regression] test: canary-apac-a10/text-gen-4k — baseline: 820 tok/s, latest: 640 tok/s, p99: 210ms -> 305ms. regression >= 15%.
arjun: Which merge? I think #4127 (kernel-selector + batching heuristics) landed yesterday afternoon. PR note said: "prefer fused_attn_v2 for short-ish sequences to cut op overhead."
dan: I can reproduce locally on an A10 node. Running the standard perf harness with the canary model gives similar numbers. Quick output:```
model=text-gen-4k device=A10 throughput=650 tok/s (was 830)
fused_attn_v2 selected for many batches; memcpy costs up 2.3x
```
katie: Can we bisect? If it's selector logic + batching interaction it might only manifest on A10 and L4 variants. apac clusters run smaller NIC drivers too which could amplify packet bursts.
arjun: Starting bisect now. Command I'm using: `git bisect start -- bad=HEAD -- good=origin/main~1 && ./scripts/run-perf --device a10 --seq 4096 --samples 50`
arjun: After halving the range, bisect points to commit `abcdef1` (author: mike) — changes: "batch padding: pad to next power-of-two, prefer short-kernel when effective seq < 2048". The padding increases effective seq seen by kernel selector.
dan: That matches my trace. Kernel selector sees padded_len ~2048 more often, picks `fused_attn_v2` which is H100-optimized and has a larger staged memcpy on A10. From `nvprof` traces: `memcpy_H2D` bursts align with RPC send bursts -> NIC tx queue spikes.
alex: We also have NIC drops in apac cluster logs around the same windows. Example from node logs:```
[03:12:21] mlx5_core: mlx5e dequeue rxq 2 overflow, drops=127
[03:12:21] cni-plugin: pod net retries=3
```
alex: Hypothesis: padding -> fused kernel -> larger device-side scatter/gather -> bigger packets/interrupt bursts -> rx/tx queue saturation on older Mellanox NICs in apac region. H100 hosts don't show the same effect because the fused kernel has a smaller memcpy pattern there.
katie: Given this is impacting canary, we should revert the batching/padding change as immediate rollback. Also add a short-term guard: make kernel-selector aware of device capability (detect A10/L4 and avoid `fused_attn_v2` there for now).
arjun: Opened revert PR #4138 (revert "batch padding: pad to next power-of-two"). Deploying to canary now.
ci-bot: rollback PR #4138 merged into deploy/canary at 1749801980 — rollout started.
dan: After the revert landed and canary rolled back, preliminary metrics: throughput back to 790 tok/s, p99 down to 220ms (roughly pre-merge baseline).
katie: Good. Follow-ups: (1) add a perf regression test in CI that runs on A10-sized instance matrix, (2) make kernel selection consider both effective_seq and device microbenchmarks (memcopy cost), (3) add NIC tx/rx queue metrics to per-cluster dashboards so we can correlate.
arjun: Also adding a unit test to the selector to surface when a kernel is faster on H100 but worse on A10. Will add a small matrix in the PR.
sofia: This is a rollout-blocker and RCA should go into the incident tracker. Thanks everyone for the quick bisect + revert. :white_check_mark:
perf-bot: Incident recorded: INC-2025-041 — root cause: batching padding + kernel-selector mismatch -> device-specific memcpy/network bursts -> NIC queue saturation on A10 clusters. Mitigation: revert + selector guard.
sofia: Please follow up with a postmortem + action items (owner, ETA) in #postmortems when you have them.
arjun: Will do — assigning owners in the PR.
